transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

The recent sink replacement does matter. Intermittent grey, smelly water after a dishwasher has apparently drained can be sink waste water running back through the dishwasher hose, particularly if the new waste connection, trap or hose routing is not right. A partial blockage in the dishwasher filter/sump is the next most likely cause; a pump or non-return valve fault is less likely when it usually drains normally. With the dishwasher switched off, look under the sink: check the drain hose is not kinked or pushed down into standing water, and run the sink tap to see whether the sink drains freely without gurgling or backing up. Does the hose join the new sink waste, and does the sink drain normally?

I had a look under the sink. Since the new sink went in, the dishwasher hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, no high loop. The sink drains a little slow. The water seems to turn up after I've drained a sink full of washing-up water.

That points to sink waste water running back into the dishwasher, rather than the dishwasher failing to drain. The hose should not lie low all the way to the spigot: it needs a high loop, clipped up beneath the worktop, before dropping down to the waste connection. The slow-draining sink also suggests the new trap or waste pipe may be partly restricted, which makes backflow more likely. With the dishwasher switched off, have the hose rerouted and securely clipped high up without kinking it; ideally ask the sink fitter to return and check/clear the trap and waste run as well. Once corrected, drain a sinkful of water and check whether water reappears in the dishwasher; if it still does, the dishwasher’s non-return valve/filter area would be the next thing to inspect.
I've looped the hose up high and clipped it under the worktop, then drained a full sink of washing-up water. No more water in the dishwasher so far. Is that all it needed?

Yes — that is very likely all the dishwasher itself needed. Leave the hose securely clipped high under the worktop, with no kinks or sagging back to the cupboard floor. As the sink is still draining a little slowly, it would still be sensible to have the trap/waste run cleared or checked; a slow waste can otherwise cause kitchen-drain problems later. If grey water returns despite the hose staying high, then the dishwasher filter and non-return valve would be the next suspects, but there is no need to investigate those now.

candidates: Sink waste connection or trap issue after the sink replacement, allowing wastewater to run back towards the dishwasher (high)
Partial blockage in the dishwasher filter, sump or drain hose (medium)
Drain pump or non-return valve not sealing reliably (low)
